description: A black horse that casts no shadow. It stamps, and the dark pools around its hooves like spilled ink.
lore: There is nothing whatever wrong with this horse. Sound feet, good coat, eats, sleeps, comes when it is called, hauls whatever you put behind it and does not sulk about the load. The only thing it does not do is lay a shadow on the ground. On a bright day people will watch the grass beside it for a while, and then find a reason to be somewhere else.

It has had a dozen owners and been handed on a dozen times, and every one of them offered a different reason out loud: too big for the yard, wrong temperament, no work for it this season. The reason none of them offered is that everybody knows which end of a long story a missing detail comes off, and a good horse you are going to have to stand and watch is worse than no horse at all.

[[characters/646b922c|Sigrun]] took it four years ago and has not handed it on. It hauls charcoal, stands in the yard behind the smithy while she works, and in the evening she scratches the place under its jaw it likes until it leans its whole considerable weight into her hand. People who know what she has already sat through in her life ask her, carefully, whether that is wise. She says the horse hauls charcoal.
gm_notes: Description adopted verbatim from the monsters agent — the art is a perfectly ordinary glossy black horse, which is exactly the point, so the observation carries it. Shortest of the five on purpose: three beats, ending on Sigrun's flat sentence rather than a summary. The record never states that a lost detail is the first stage of thinning; the dread of the dozen owners demonstrates it. Sigrun keeping it is a quiet echo of B11 (revealed) and should stay glancing.
